scope: dos.zone mainstream original DOS releases — base-game listings only. Mods, forks, fan remakes, expansions, compilation bundles and uncertain entries excluded.
requestedBy: user (explicit request for a mainstream DOS batch); no assistant or user review is recorded here.

source.urlDiscovery: https://dos.zone/sitemap.xml (297,423 bytes, 2,530 <loc> URLs) saved to artifacts/research/dos-zone/sitemap.xml and urls.txt
source.method: direct HTTPS GET (desktop Chrome UA) of each candidate page, saving body + response headers to artifacts/research/dos-zone/<slug>.html and <slug>.hdr; Agent Reach/Jina Reader rendering was used for the earlier Doom entry and was not re-run for this batch

verificationLimits: No gameplay was executed. Every entry is verified only as 'a live dos.zone launch page exposing a js-dos bundle reference'. HTTP 200 alone was never treated as proof of gameplay, and one HTTP 200 page (Grand Theft Auto 1997) was rejected precisely because it exposed no bundle.
No assistant review and no user review is recorded in this file. Discovery/research is not approval.

No permission to host, stream, frame or monetise these destinations is asserted. The pages' own CSP frame-ancestors headers restrict framing to dos.zone-owned origins, which is evidence AGAINST naive iframe embedding in Gameflex, not for it.
CSP/X-Frame-Options observations were read from the saved response headers only; no browser rendering test was performed.

entries.title: DOOM
entries.description: The 1993 id Software original (slugs/dated title 'DOOM', page slug encodes Dec 1993).
entries.requirements: Desktop browser with keyboard and mouse; page also advertises a multiplayer play-online door.
entries.browserEvidence: Direct HTTPS GET of https://dos.zone/doom-dec-1993/ with a desktop Chrome UA returned HTTP 200 (37818 bytes). The page markup contains a live js-dos host block: <div class="jsdos wh-full z-10" data-url="https://cdn.dos.zone/custom/dos/doom.jsdos"> plus js-dos controls, i.e. the page declares the DOS bundle it would run. Page copy states its games are 'free and without ads on dos.zone'. Launch-UI/bundle markup only — the emulator was never booted and no gameplay was observed.
issues: Bundle is a generic doom.jsdos with no edition marker; whether the hosted build is shareware or the full registered release is unverified.
Page advertises an online multiplayer door; netplay was not exercised and support for this specific game is not established by that link.

Embedding in the Gameflex player is not permitted by the page's own CSP: frame-ancestors allowlists dos.zone, cdn.dos.zone, sec.dos.zone, test.js-dos.com and discord.com only, so a Gameflex iframe would be blocked. Not inferring any hosting/streaming permission from this or from absent X-Frame-Options.

Playability is NOT verified: only the launch page and its bundle reference were observed. The js-dos emulator was never booted and no gameplay, input or save behaviour was tested. HTTP 200 does not prove the game runs.
Third-party emulation host (dos.zone, js-dos/dosbox). Distribution rights and the hosted build's provenance are unverified; dos.zone publishes a DMCA page but that does not establish permission.
Exact edition/build hosted (shareware vs full, regions, bundled content) is not established by the page markup and is marked unverified.
Bundle is fetched from cdn.dos.zone / br.cdn.dos.zone at play time, so first launch depends on that CDN and on host CPU for emulation performance.
